papers.title_in_file: Building a Quantum Engineering Undergraduate Program
papers.version_note: The text is the arXiv preprint 2108.01311v1 (3 Aug 2021). The file name carries 2022, the year of the published version.
papers.what_it_is: A multi-author roadmap for undergraduate quantum engineering education: a first QISE course built from modules, a minor and a track, a diversity plan, and hands-on hardware training.

existing.value: The authors state that they define quantum engineering as the application of engineering methods and principles to quantum information systems and problems.
quotes: we deﬁne quantum engineering as the application of engineering methods and principles to quantum information systems and problems.
existing.certainty_reason: The authors give the definition in Section I (p.3) as their own.

existing.note: The paper limits the recommendation: it is for creating quantum-proficient engineers and is tied to the current stage of the quantum industry. The paper also says full degrees may be desired later. The quote is in the Section VII bullets on p.21, not p.22.
existing.value: The authors recommend that universities and colleges develop new minors in quantum engineering or tracks embedded in traditional majors, rather than full undergraduate degree programs, to create quantum-proficient engineers at the current stage of the quantum industry.
quotes: To create quantum-proﬁcient engineers at a higher level than just being quantum aware

at the current stage of the quantum industry, we recommend universities and colleges develop new minors in quantum engineering or tracks embedded in traditional majors, rather than full undergraduate degree programs.
existing.certainty_reason: The authors' own recommendation, not tested in the paper.

existing.value: The authors state that their recommendations ultimately reflect only the authors, although they draw heavily on community input.
quotes: Our recommendations, although ultimately reﬂecting only the authors, draw heavily on community input.

existing.note: Section VII (p.21) repeats the point for programs and courses in general.

assertions.value: The authors state that both the RVNN and the CVNN are fully connected sequence-to-sequence networks of five layers (one input layer, three hidden layers and one output layer); the RVNN uses real weights, biases and ReLU, the CVNN uses complex weights, biases and a complex ReLU (CReLU) that applies ReLU separately to the real and imaginary components, and the CVNN parameter count was capped at a level approximately equal to or below the RVNN's.
quotes: Both models adopt a fully connected sequence-to-sequence architecture consisting of ﬁve layers: one input layer, three hidden layers, and one output layer.
combined with a complex ReLU (CReLU) activation function that applies the ReLU operation separately to the real and imaginary components.
we capped the number of trainable parameters in the CVNN at a level approximately equal to or below that of the RVNN.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own architecture in Section IV.

assertions.value: The authors state that the RVNN treats the real and imaginary components of each off-diagonal element as separate real degrees of freedom, while the CVNN encodes the upper-triangular reduced density matrix directly as a complex vector, embedding each real diagonal entry as a + ia at the input and discarding that additive phase at the output.
assertions.anchor: Section II.A, PDF p.2 to p.3
quotes: the real and imaginary components akl, bkl are treated as separate degrees of freedom
We encode the upper-triangular RDM directly as a complex vector
we embed them uniformly into C by mapping a → a + ia at the input; at the output, this additive phase is discarded to maintain Hermiticity.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section II.A defines both encodings.
assertions.reader_inference: The CVNN layer in Eq. 12 is a real block matrix with the structure [[Wr, -Wi], [Wi, Wr]] acting on the stacked real and imaginary parts, which is a weight-tied special case of the general real layer in Eq. 10. With ReLU applied channelwise in both models, the CVNN is a parameter-tied real network; the paper does not test whether the gain comes from the tying or from the complex arithmetic.

assertions.value: The authors state that the upper-triangular representation enforces Hermiticity by construction, the lower triangle being recovered by conjugation.
quotes: and enforces Hermiticity by construction (the lower triangle is recovered by conjugation).

assertions.reader_inference: The representation is described for the density matrix in general, so Hermiticity of the output holds for both models by construction. A search of the text finds no Hermiticity measurement in the Results.

assertions.value: The authors state that no RVNN can generate such rotations in a single step, because real weights act independently on the real and imaginary channels.
quotes: No RVNN can generate such rotations in a single step, because real weights act independently on Re and Im channels
assertions.reader_inference: The RVNN layer in Eq. 10 uses a full real weight matrix on the stacked real and imaginary inputs, and Eq. 12 shows the complex multiplication is itself a real matrix of that kind. So a real layer can represent the rotation and scaling; the statement holds only if real weights act channel by channel, which Eq. 10 does not say.
